title: Grateful Dead Live at KQED Studios on 1970-08-30
lineage: FM > Sony TC-366 Reel (concert polyester tape) > CDx3 > HP 9350i > EAC v0.9b4 > CD Wave v1.6 > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality matrix recording captures a standout Easy Wind jam and the first slowed‑down Candyman, but overall sound is muddied and uneven.
ai_review.review: The short studio set shines on tracks like Easy Wind, Candyman and Brokedown Palace, with Jerry’s vocals getting particular praise. Technically the recording suffers from muddiness, low‑bass mix issues and odd quad‑channel quirks that make parts of it sound “crappy,” limiting its listenability despite the strong performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers love the musical moments (average 4‑5 stars for performance) while several note serious recording flaws, yielding a weighted average around 4.0–4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muddied and distorted spots; Phil’s bass mixed too low; quad‑channel split creates uneven balance; overall sound is okay but far from pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A brief studio‑session set that moves from the high‑energy Easy Wind jam to a newly‑slowed Candyman and ends with a beautiful Brokedown Palace, showcasing early 1970 Dead chemistry despite the uneven recording.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s voice is highlighted as mesmerizing on Brokedown Palace and praised on Candyman.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is mixed too low, detracting from the overall balance.
